title: Gnocchi alla Sorrentina
subtitle: potato gnocchi baked in tomato sauce with mozzarella
excerpt: Gnocchi alla sorrentina is a Campanian dish of soft potato gnocchi cooked in a simple tomato and basil sauce, topped with mozzarella and parmesan, then baked until bubbling and golden. Making the gnocchi from scratch takes time but the result is far softer than anything from a packet. Serves 4.
sourceNotes: Gnocchi alla sorrentina takes its name from Sorrento on the Amalfi Coast, where this baked version of gnocchi al pomodoro is a local institution. The combination of soft gnocchi, sharp tomato sauce and melted mozzarella is a hallmark of Campanian cooking. The dish is typically finished in a terracotta pot called a pignatiello.

glossaryTerms.definition: Small Italian dumplings most commonly made from potato and flour, boiled until they float then sauced or baked.
In the style of Sorrento, typically referring to a preparation of gnocchi baked with tomato sauce and mozzarella from the Campanian coastal town.

content.text: themselves: floury potatoes are baked or boiled until dry, riced while hot, then mixed with just enough flour to hold together without becoming dense. The critical technique is using as little flour as possible. Too much and the gnocchi become heavy; too little and they fall apart in the water. Serves 4.

The gnocchi are boiled just until they float, then tossed in tomato sauce before going into the baking dish. The mozzarella goes on top and the whole thing bakes for 15 minutes until the cheese is melted and patchy with golden spots.

Cook the potatoes in their skins in boiling water for 25 to 30 minutes until completely tender. Drain and peel while hot. Pass through a ricer or mash until completely smooth with no lumps. Spread on a tray and leave to steam dry for 5 minutes.

Tip the potato onto a floured surface. Add the beaten egg and most of the flour. Work together gently until a soft dough forms. Add more flour sparingly if the dough sticks. Do not overwork. Season to taste.
Divide the dough into portions and roll each into a rope about 2cm thick. Cut into 2cm lengths. Roll each piece over the back of a fork to create ridges if you like, or leave them plain.

Make the tomato sauce: heat the olive oil in a saucepan. Add the whole garlic cloves and cook for 2 minutes. Add the tinned tomatoes, season to taste and simmer for 15 minutes. Remove the garlic. Stir in most of the basil.

Heat the oven to 200°C (fan 180°C / Gas 6). Bring a large pot of water to the boil. Cook the gnocchi in batches: drop them in and remove each one with a slotted spoon about 30 seconds after it floats to the surface.
Toss the boiled gnocchi in most of the tomato sauce. Transfer to a baking dish. Spoon over the remaining sauce. Scatter the mozzarella and parmesan on top.
Bake for 15 minutes until the cheese is melted and golden in spots. Scatter the remaining basil leaves on top and serve immediately.

attrs.cause: Too much flour was added or the potatoes were watery
attrs.fix: Use floury potatoes and dry them well after boiling. Add flour gradually and stop as soon as the dough holds together

attrs.symptom: Gnocchi fall apart in the boiling water
attrs.cause: The dough was too wet or under-floured
attrs.fix: Test one gnocco first. If it dissolves, knead in a little more flour and test again before cooking the rest

attrs.symptom: Mozzarella makes the dish watery in the oven
attrs.cause: Fresh mozzarella releases a lot of liquid when baked
attrs.fix: Tear the mozzarella and leave it on kitchen paper for 30 minutes before using to draw out some of the whey

content.text: This dish comes from Sorrento and the Amalfi Coast in Campania. It is a Sunday lunch dish in the region, made when there is time to prepare the gnocchi from scratch. In Neapolitan restaurants it is often served in the terracotta pot it was baked in, brought straight to the table. The tomato sauce stays simple so the potato gnocchi and melted mozzarella are the focus.
